exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Hong Kong Tower, Cathay two five one, late downwind Runway zero sev-en right, request touch-and-go.
exchanges.meaning: Requests a touch-and-go while late downwind for Runway 07R.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, Hong Kong Tower, number two following Diamond four zero on two mile final, report final.
exchanges.meaning: Sequences Cathay 251 as number two behind Diamond 40 on a two-mile final and asks it to report final.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Number two, follow Diamond, report final, Cathay two five one.
exchanges.meaning: Readback of the number-two sequence and the report-final instruction.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Hong Kong Tower, Cathay two five one, final Runway zero sev-en right, touch-and-go.
exchanges.meaning: Reports final for Runway 07R intending a touch-and-go.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, wind zero six zero degrees wun zero knots, Runway zero sev-en right, cleared touch-and-go.
exchanges.meaning: Passes the surface wind and issues the touch-and-go clearance for Runway 07R.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Wind zero six zero at wun zero, Runway zero sev-en right, cleared touch-and-go, Cathay two five one.
exchanges.meaning: Readback of the wind and the touch-and-go clearance.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, go around immediately, aircraft stopped on runway!
exchanges.meaning: Orders an immediate go-around because an aircraft has stopped on the runway.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Going around immediately, Cathay two five one.
exchanges.meaning: Readback of the immediate go-around instruction.

vocabulary.definition: Authorization to land and take off without stopping or vacating.
Authorization to land, come to a complete stop, and take off. Requires substantial runway length.
Approach over runway without touching down on the surface. Used during instrument training.
Direction of standard circuit/pattern turns. Defines circuit direction.
Mandatory command to abort landing due to runway obstruction.

quiz.question: What is the primary operational difference between a "Touch-and-Go" and a "Stop-and-Go" clearance?
options: A touch-and-go is only permitted for twin-engine aircraft.
A touch-and-go takes off immediately after touchdown without stopping; a stop-and-go comes to a complete halt on the runway before taking off again.
A stop-and-go requires vacating the runway and taxiing back.
quiz.explanation: Under standard ATC definitions, a touch-and-go consists of landing and taking off without coming to a stop. A stop-and-go involves bringing the aircraft to a full stop on the runway before applying takeoff thrust.

quiz.question: What is the flight crew required to do if an air traffic controller commands "Go around immediately, aircraft on runway" while the aircraft is in the landing flare?
options: Apply full go-around power immediately, pitch up to establish a climb, retract flaps in stages, and climb straight ahead or follow published missed approach instructions.
Land firmly on the runway and apply maximum brakes.
Shut down engines to prevent collision.
quiz.explanation: An immediate go-around instruction in the landing flare requires immediate application of maximum go-around thrust, arresting descent, establishing a positive rate of climb, and retracting drag devices in stages.

sections.heading: Section 2: Core Learning Content & Vocabulary Table
sections.body: Cleared touch-and-go — Authorization to land and take off without stopping or vacating. "Runway 07R, cleared touch-and-go." / Cleared stop-and-go — Authorization to land, come to a complete stop, and take off. Requires substantial runway length! / Cleared low approach — Approach over runway without touching down on the surface. Used during instrument training. / Make left / right traffic — Direction of standard circuit/pattern turns. Defines circuit direction. / Go around immediately — Mandatory command to abort landing due to runway obstruction. Preceding traffic stalled on runway!

sections.heading: Section 8: Spaced Repetition Review Drill
sections.body: Day 37 Review (+1d): Landing clearances require an explicit "Runway 07L, cleared to land". Strict 10-knot certified tailwind limit. Day 35 Review (+3d): If visual reference is lost while circling, execute an immediate climbing turn toward the landing runway to remain within protected obstacle clearance.

sections.heading: Section 9: Fun Aviation Fact — "Hands Off the Gear Handle"
sections.body: During flight training, touch-and-goes are notorious for accidental gear retractions on the ground! In the rush to reconfigure flaps during a high-speed rollout, nervous pilots have accidentally grabbed the landing gear lever instead of the flap handle, collapsing the gear and belly-landing on the runway! Flight instructors teach the golden rule: eyes confirmed on the flap lever, and NEVER touch the gear handle until positive rate of climb is established!
